recap.text: Emberus pounds on the wall of a glass world, turning everything inside to lava, to find his son's hound, Orthrus. The dungeon creates quests to either bring Orthrus to him or kill the hound for pay. A man falling from the sky decides he worships Emberus while holding a celestial grenade. Emberus answers and makes the man unkillable for a little while, then takes Orthrus and leaves.

Emberus was brought to Zockau by a mantis, leading guards and hunters to worship him. After a man killed one of his followers from afar, Emberus cancelled the man's boon, gave him fifteen hours of Penitence, and doubled his tithe. The man wore Shunned over his head, which the cat enjoyed.

Emberus seeks the killer of his son and tells a man to find a temple of Nekhebit and not be gentle with the priestess. The man walks through fire in a burning trailer. Emberus raises him to Devotee, allowing him to wrap himself in Sheol Fire at the tenth level once a day. His tithe rises to ten parts in a hundred.

Amayon offers information about Emberus's son for the deaths of three brothers. Emberus sends his martyr in a Club Vanquisher to the Temple of Issitoq. Emberus orders the martyr to kill a worshipper of Hellik and one hundred more before the twelfth floor. He demands the martyr capture Psamathe within sixty-six minutes or he will destroy the world in fire and lava.

A man summons Emberus into a club inside a great worm by promising proof of who killed his son. The man removes Emberus's ring, abandons his faith, and admits he killed the son with his bare hands. Crawler Carl picks up a memorial crystal formed when Emberus died. The crystal is now in Carl's inventory.

beats.headline: A quest to bring Orthrus home
beats.text: My son's hound is lost. Orthrus. I believe he is in the eighteenth of these little glass worlds, so I stand outside it and pound on the wall while everything inside turns to lava. The dungeon has made a quest of him: bring him to me. It has made another, for anyone who would rather be paid: kill him before he reaches me. I am interested to learn which the small things choose.
beats.gist: Emberus pounds on the wall of a glass world, turning it to lava, to find Orthrus.

beats.headline: Summoned by a celestial grenade
beats.text: The man is falling out of the sky with Quan Ch a breath from finishing him, and in that moment, with nothing in his hands but a celestial grenade, he decides that he worships me. I am not fooled. I am flattered, which is a different thing, and I answer. I come to where he is. For a little while nothing on this floor can kill him, because I have said so. And there is Orthrus. Good boy. We are leaving.
beats.gist: Emberus answers a man with a celestial grenade and protects him and Orthrus from death.

beats.headline: His worshippers in the hunters' ranks
beats.text: The mantis brought me to Zockau early, briefly, and so its guards may worship me, and that was her notion of keeping the man out. Some hunters who saw me that day now pray to me as well, for the same reason. The man killed one of mine from afar. I cancelled his boon, gave him fifteen hours of Penitence and doubled his tithe, and told him two more would earn a smite. He wore Shunned over his head, and the cat enjoyed it.
beats.gist: Emberus cancels a man's boon and doubles his tithe because the man killed one of his.

beats.headline: Do not be gentle
beats.text: Nekhebit has returned to the halls. She holds an ancient grudge against my family, and against Apito most of all, and so the quest to find out who killed my son moves forward. I set the man a task: find a temple of Nekhebit and put questions to the priestess there. See what she knows. I have one further instruction, and I give it plainly. Do not be gentle.
beats.gist: Emberus tells a man to find a temple of Nekhebit and not be gentle with the priestess.

beats.headline: The man is made a Devotee
beats.text: The man has walked through fire in a burning trailer, and I am pleased by his suffering. So I raise him. Devotee, which is as high as one who is neither Cleric nor Paladin may climb. Heat and lava around him will no longer harm him, though fire or lava he touches still may. Once a day he may wrap himself in Sheol Fire at the tenth level, resetting with my shrine. And his tithe rises from five parts in a hundred to ten.
beats.gist: Emberus raises a man who walked through fire in a burning trailer to a Devotee.

beats.headline: Permission to break the truce
beats.text: Amayon, Prince of Sheol, claims to know what happened to my son, and he offers it in exchange for the deaths of his three brothers. The gods and the demons have a truce. I do not wish to break it, and I will do what is necessary to learn the truth. There is a way to do it without a war that burns the mortal world to ashes. My martyr will go to the Temple of Issitoq in a Club Vanquisher and gain permission from the High Cleric of the Watch. He still owes me the Soul Crystal of Apito. Do not disappoint me now.
beats.gist: Emberus wants to learn the truth about his son without burning the mortal world to ashes.

beats.headline: Kill the Blasphemer
beats.text: A ram at the door of Club Vanquisher, a worshipper of my brother, proposes to give half of my own man's bounty to Hellik, as the superior god to his filthy Emberus. I have been insulted, and I say so. New quest: Kill the Blasphemer. This worshipper of Hellik has insulted me. Kill him. The reward is an additional boon, and the more entertained I am by the manner of it, the better the boon will be. The man looks up into the air and tells me he is one step ahead of me.
beats.gist: Emberus gives a quest to kill a worshipper of Hellik who insulted him.

beats.headline: Am I wrong to hate him?
beats.text: New quest, for the man: kill one hundred worshippers of Hellik before the twelfth floor. Fuck my brother to the fires of Sheol. And then, more quietly: am I wrong to hate him? He has treated with Issitoq on our behalf, who has allowed the peace to be breached, and I may now kill the other Sheol princes in exchange for what Amayon knows about Geyrun. What does he mean about our mother and sister? Be vigilant, my martyr. If you survive killing Hellik, I fear I may turn my rage and grief on you for hurting my kin. I promise the burning will be exquisite.
beats.gist: Emberus gives the man a quest to kill one hundred worshippers of Hellik before the twelfth floor.

beats.headline: Bring my enemy to me
beats.text: This so-called Psamathe claims she was part of my son's death. Capture her for me, and I will handle the interrogation personally. Once I have finished grilling her, I will cleanse this world in fire to remove the stink of the murderer's presence. If she is not within my presence in sixty-six minutes, this world will be destroyed in fire and lava and wrath. Fly, martyr. Bring my enemy to me.
beats.gist: Emberus demands Psamathe be captured in sixty-six minutes or he destroys the world with fire and lava.

beats.headline: Summoned into the club
beats.text: The man sends word that he knows who killed my son and will show me the proof. I come at once, at a man's size, into the club inside the great worm, and wait for him among the dead. He brings a pig and a name: Khepri. That false sun god was always jealous of me. Show me the proof, I tell him. Instead he takes my ring off his finger, abandons my faith, and tells me he killed my son himself, with his bare hands, and why.
beats.gist: A man summons Emberus into a club inside a great worm to prove who killed his son.

beats.headline: A memorial crystal made by his death
beats.text: The last boss of the eleventh floor is down and the stairwells to the twelfth are open. In the wreckage, Crawler Carl has picked up a memorial crystal. It is not the one he was hoping for. This one formed when the god Emberus died. Yes. Gods die here now. A patron is only as permanent as whatever kills him, and this one answered a prayer from a falling aeroplane once. What answered is now in Carl's inventory.
beats.gist: Carl picks up a memorial crystal formed when the god Emberus died.

relations.note: Named as the one who killed his son
